title: Graduated Credit Accelerator & Contract SQ Readiness
creator: Avery Kaplan
body:
Summary:
This ticket scopes an integrated experiment that combines a graduated credit allocation model ("accelerator") for self-serve and trial accounts with a parallel enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) readiness stream to shorten contract cycles for teams that convert during or immediately after trials. The goal is to improve PLG conversion velocity while keeping unit economics and support load under control.

Background & Motivation:
Current trial mechanics grant a flat credit allotment with a fixed expiration. We see trade-offs: generous time-based credits increase runway but raise fraud/low-quality usage and cost; smaller immediate credits increase friction and reduce product engagement. Separately, enterprise prospects routinely stall on the security questionnaire and contract back-and-forth after a promising trial engagement. The two problems are correlated — higher-engagement trials often need faster legal/infosec cycles to convert.

Hypothesis:
1) A graduated-credit accelerator that increases credit capacity conditioned on engagement milestones (e.g., 10K tokens consumed in the first 7 days unlocks +50% credits and access to advanced rate limits) will increase engaged-trial conversion rate by >=35% versus a flat-credit control.
2) Pairing accelerated credit unlocks with an SQ "fast-track" pack (pre-populated, owner-mapped answers + named legal contact + standard data processing addendum template) for qualifying trials will reduce time-to-sign for SMB/upper-mid-market deals by >=25%.

Experiment Design:
- Arms:
  - Control: existing flat-credit, fixed 30-day expiry (current baseline).
  - Arm A: Graduated accelerator — initial small credit bucket (X credits) + conditional unlocks tied to event thresholds (usage, verified email/SSO, workspace creation). Unlocks extend expiry and add temporary quota increases rather than permanent grants.
  - Arm B: Arm A + SQ fast-track package eligible for workspaces that hit qualifying engagement thresholds and indicate company size > 20 employees via signup form.
- Target cohorts: new self-serve signups and trial invites from marketing campaigns, randomized at signup. Exclude known internal/test accounts and partners.
- Canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> full within 3 weeks if no regressions. Separate rollout for enterprises invited by AE with SSO-enabled trials (manual enrollment).

Success Metrics & Signals:
Primary metrics (relative lift versus control):
- Trial->Paid conversion within 60 days (target: +35% for Arm B, +20% for Arm A)
- Time-to-first-pay or signed contract (median days, target: -25% for Arm B)
- Engaged DAU/WAU for trial workspaces in first 14 days (target: +15%)
Secondary metrics (safety/economics):
- Cost per converted customer (CPC) delta (acceptable increase <= 15%)
- Abuse/fraud signals (new account rate, spike in suspicious patterns) — must remain within baseline +10%
- Support & legal throughput (requests requiring manual SQ effort) — expect decrease for Arm B

Instrumentation & Dashboards:
- New A/B flags in Redwood backend to identify cohort (experiment_id: PM-9981-accel-v1).
- Dashboards: conversion funnel, token consumption histogram, unlock event timeline, SQ packet downloads and AE handoffs. Link to draft dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/pm-9981 (placeholder).
- Alerts: automated rollback if conversion drops >10% or abuse signals exceed threshold.

SQ Readiness Workstream (parallel tasks for enterprise):
- Create an "SQ fast-track" one-pager and a pre-filled questionnaire template mapped to internal owners (security, infra, legal, data). Owners and SLAs documented in CON-SEC-2025/PM-9981.
- Legal to approve a standard DPA and contract language for trial-extension/purchase conversion (owner: Priya Menon, target legal sign-off by 2025-02-24).
- Build a simple portal flow for qualifying prospects to request the fast-track package; integrate with AE handoff and CRM (Salesforce).

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Credits vs. quota: prefer temporary quota lifts over permanent credit grants to avoid long-term cost leakage. Unlocked capacity must timebox and be revokable.
- Anti-abuse: require at least one verification step (email + domain check or SSO) before certain unlocks. Consider rate-limiting per new workspace ID.
- UX: minimize cognitive load — show a progress bar for unlock milestones and explicit messaging about how additional credits are earned and expire.

Open Questions / Decisions Needed:
- Exact thresholds for unlocks (tokens consumed, number of completions) — initial proposal: 10k tokens in 7 days -> +50% credits; 25k tokens -> temporary quota bump + access to advanced prompts. Decision owner: Riya.
- Pricing model for converted accounts that used unlocked credits — should unlocked usage be billed normally post-conversion or prorated? Finance input required.
- Which enterprise segments qualify for SQ fast-track? Recommend <500 employees for self-service fast-track; >500 handled by AE/enterprise channel.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive unlocks drive cost > revenue. Mitigation: temporary/timeboxed unlocks + canary with cost gating, real-time alerts to Product/Finance.
- Risk: legal churn from multiple ad-hoc contract changes. Mitigation: single approved DPA template and AE playbook.

Timeline & Milestones:
- 2025-02-12: Kickoff (done)
- 2025-02-14: Engineering design review + instrumentation plan (done)
- 2025-02-17: Legal draft of DPA & SQ template (draft complete)
- 2025-02-20: Small-scale canary (1%) goes live for self-serve signups (In Progress)
- 2025-02-28: Evaluate canary metrics; decide 5% expansion
- 2025-03-03: Full experiment rollout decision / target completion

Links & Artifacts:
- PRD (draft): https://confluence.redwood.internal/pm/PM-9981
- SQ template: https://drive.redwood.internal/pm-9981-sq-template.docx
- Engineering RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/321

Next Steps (short term):
- Finish threshold tuning with Eng (Riya + Tomas) by 2025-02-22.
- Send SQ packet to legal owners for final review (Avery).
- Monitor canary daily and collect qualitative feedback from AE team on Arm B handoffs.
comments: 2025-02-12 — Kickoff meeting: aligned on goals, owners assigned. Action: Eng to prepare feature flags and telemetry; Legal to draft DPA.

2025-02-14 — Engineering design review completed. Decided temporary quota lifts vs. permanent credits; implement TTL for all unlocks (default 14 days). Tomas noted cache and rate-limit changes required in runtime; ENG ticket ENG-2129 opened.
2025-02-17 — Legal draft of DPA and SQ template shared. Priya requested two clarifications on data retention language; Avery to follow up. Legal estimates 3 business days for final review.
2025-02-18 — UX review: progress bar copy simplified. Suggestion: call the unlocks 'Accelerator Milestones' instead of 'credits' to emphasize earned runway. Design to supply variant for A/B test.
2025-02-20 — Canary 1% launched for self-serve. Early telemetry shows 8% higher 7-day engagement for Arm A and 12% for Arm B; sample size small. Monitoring hooked to alerts.
